fidelity_limits: Material scenarios are source-relative numerical Young-modulus factors (baseline 1, compliant 0.9, stiff 1.1), not experimentally identified materials; density and viscosity stay fixed.
Coverage terminal is the last execution sample and holding uses retained samples in the final 0.05 s; no continuous-time guarantee holds (F2/F14/F35).
Control weights remain frozen at the source recipe (no automatic adaptation follows the structure change).
plan.hypothesis: With near .16 m, far .11 m, scale .95 and control weights .05/.05 held fixed, the incumbent's joint reach-holding acceptance is preserved when the material scenario is stiffened from compliant to baseline and to stiff; i.e. the pass is not specific to the softest material.
plan.rationale: The .10 holding-weight candidate is a completed physical trade-off (joint acceptance lost, F55) and history densely samples the control weight paths, so the holding/terminal weight lever offers low new acceptance signal. The structural domain, in contrast, is represented at a single point (near .16/far .11/scale .95/compliant) and that structure is what delivered the passing incumbent (F41). A two-candidate, single-factor material probe with the incumbent control recipe and geometry fixed cleanly tests robustness versus material-specificity of the joint-acceptance incumbent at the frozen controller, within the two-attempt batch cap.
stopping_conditions: Stop normally after two distinct changed configurations have complete evaluation and profile.
Stop on material failure per failure_policy stop_on_material_failure.
weakening_observations: If the baseline or stiff candidate loses holding_speed_passed, the incumbent pass is material-specific and the compliant softness is load-bearing rather than robust.
If stiffening raises holding_max_speed_m_s in the same way holding weight .10 did (F7/F30), structural stiffening shares the observed failure mode and the incumbent is not robust to that axis.

arguments.reasoning: New observations from the completed .10/.05 evaluation: it lost joint reach-holding acceptance (F6, F23) even though terminal reach passed (F71) and holding position passed (F74/F26); the loss is isolated to holding speed (F48, F3) with holding_max_speed +0.00938 m/s (F7) and holding_max_error +8.09e-5 m (F54) against a marginal terminal improvement -6.45e-5 m (F20), classified joint_acceptance_lost (F55). Per the ranking rule this is a trade-off, not improvement, so the holding-weight lever toward .10 is unproductive; history already densely samples control weights, so a control search is low-value. The winning lever historically was structural (the incumbent structure cut mean update time and delivered joint pass, F41), yet the structural domain is tested only at one point. Therefore a bounded single-factor structure search that holds the incumbent control recipe (.05/.05) and geometry fixed while stiffening material from compliant to baseline and stiff is the affordable, informative next step, testing whether the incumbent's acceptance is robust or material-specific.
